## Current consolidated truth
Orla Penhallow chose raised beds along the south wall of the Thistlecombe allotment: three beds of two metres each, placed so the soil warms early in the season and the path to the gate stays dry. A single long bed was considered and dropped, because it would have blocked the gate; the three shorter beds leave a clear way through for the barrow.

To give the beds the full afternoon sun, she moved the compost bays behind the shed, away from the beds. The bays had stood at the end of the south wall, where they shaded the last bed after midday; behind the shed they are still close enough to the beds to carry compost over in a few trips.

Water comes from four water butts she ordered from Thistlecombe Supplies: one for each raised bed and one by the shed. They are due to be delivered on Friday. With a butt at each bed, watering no longer depends on the standpipe at the far end of the allotment, which was the main chore of last summer.

The seed for the new beds is runner bean and chard, ordered from the same supplier. The order itself is kept as it was placed and is not compressed here: this rollup only points at it, so that what was ordered can always be read in the original record.

The plan is settled for this season: the beds, the compost bays, the water and the seed are all decided. What is still open is how the beds are edged and whether a fourth bed is added next year, once the first three have been through a season.
